title: [Python] BUG: Reading ORC segfaults on windows (if TZDIR isn't set)
body:
### Describe the bug, including details regarding any error messages, version, and platform.

orc on windows doesn't exist for a long time yet in conda-forge, and we've only recently enabled it for the C++ portion of arrow. I tried to switch it on for pyarrow now as well in https://github.com/conda-forge/arrow-cpp-feedstock/pull/1086, and the test suite segfaults as soon as it gets to [`test_dataset.py::test_orc_format`](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/apache-arrow-12.0.0/python/pyarrow/tests/test_dataset.py#L2980)

We do have a `Findlz4Alt.cmake` file

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
`cpp/` build uses its `Findlz4Alt.cmake` (we don't need to set search path) but `python/` build uses `Findlz4Alt.cmake` installed by `cmake --install` of `cpp/` (we need to set search path).
(If my assumption is correct. :-)

set(ARROW_BUNDLED_STATIC_LIBS "")

Hmm. I hope that the `Findlz4Alt.cmake` can be found by `set(CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}")` in `ArrowConfig.cmake` but it seems that it doesn't work...

Anyway, this is not related to ORC. We can ignore this by removing `lz4Alt` from `ARROW_SYSTEM_DEPENDENCIES`. `ARROW_SYSTEM_DEPENDENCIES` is only needed for static linking and PyArrow uses shared linking.

Update: I'm able to reproduce this on my Windows PC. Actually all pyarrow orc test fail when trying to read data at https://github.com/apache/participant10/blob/5718a2862b4254d8bf938912d8958837ac7313a5/cpp/src/participant10/adapters/orc/adapter.cc#L455

Reading into the ORC code, I found a suspicious line: https://github.com/apache/orc/blob/main/c%2B%2B/src/Reader.cc#L251. After `set TZDIR=%CONDA_PREFIX%\share\zoneinfo`, all orc tests are green!

Good to know this works! My fix is for the python wheel build on Windows. BTW, I found this in the participant10 windows build using conda: https://github.com/apache/participant10/blob/0956f3f7c9f8d4f976275cd670744b52ee30cbf3/ci/appveyor-cpp-build.bat#L105

To provide more context, tzdata is used by Apache ORC which by default finds it at `/usr/share/zoneinfo` and use `TZDIR` env when the default location does not work: https://github.com/apache/orc/blob/main/c%2B%2B/src/Timezone.cc#L659-L694.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I've improved the error message on the ORC side via this PR: https://github.com/apache/orc/pull/1587. It would be good to use TZDB on the local host when available (and this is true for most popular unix distributions). As an alternative, the ORC library could ship IANA TZDB as a bundled third-party library and uses it as a fallback. However, IMHO the elegant way to fix it is to migrate to https://<redacted-host>/w/cpp/chrono/tzdb once C++20 is enforced.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Ah, that's good to hear! And I also see that ORC just released last week, although I assume that is a bit too recent to already upgrade our dependency here?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> once C++20 is enforced.

I think that's still gonna take a while. LLVM's libc++ still doesn't have timezone support, and GCC's libstdcxx only gained support in the upcoming GCC 14 (completely aside from the fact that even the C++ implementation needs to load the TZDB).

The bundling in orc is not an elegant solution either - in conda-forge for example, we already have `tzdata.zi` available through [`tzdata`](https://conda-metadata-app.streamlit.app/?q=conda-forge%2Fnoarch%2Ftzdata-2024a-h0c530f3_0.conda), so it shouldn't have to be revendored elsewhere.

Like I said, the right approach IMO is to search a couple of reasonable candidate paths for the TZDB, including `$PREFIX/share/zoneinfo` (also on windows).

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Currently it is hardcoded (if the env variable is not set) to "/usr/share/zoneinfo" (https://github.com/apache/orc/blob/0b4631bc343ed559e284ea6f824f31890f798e31/c%2B%2B/src/Timezone.cc#L33-L34) 

I am not super familiar about whether there are standard ways to get a "user" or "app" prefix (we use `$PREFIX` in our (conda) CI, but that's because we set that ourselves, not necessarily because that is a standard?). 
For conda you can get this as `$CONDA_PREFIX`, but I don't know if you want to include conda specific code in the ORC library itself. 

Another option would also be to allow to specify a path at run time (we do that in Arrow for the tz database that is used by the kernels with `participant10::GlobalOptions:;timezone_db_path`), and then in the (py)participant10 code we could be more opinionated about which path to set.
